profile.name: Spiral Dance
profile.tagline: A Neopagan line dance of interlocking spirals, raising power and honoring the dead.
profile.insight: In 1979 in Berkeley, California, Starhawk and the Reclaiming movement performed the first Spiral Dance to mark the publication of her book and meld art, music, and politics.
profile.profile: The Spiral Dance is a traditional Neopagan ceremonial group dance practiced primarily in the United States, particularly within feminist Wicca and the Reclaiming tradition. Originating in Berkeley, California, in 1979, the dance is designed to raise ritual power, emphasize community, and celebrate rebirth. Dancers hold hands in a continuous line and execute a grapevine step led by a facilitator who spirals inward counter-clockwise, then turns outward to weave clockwise. This winding structure brings every participant face-to-face with every other dancer in the spiral.
profile.profile_long:
The Spiral Dance is a traditional Neopagan group dance practiced in the United States, especially within feminist Wicca and the Reclaiming movement. The dance was first performed in Berkeley, California, in 1979 during a ritual conceived to meld art, music, and politics while celebrating the publication of the book The Spiral Dance by Starhawk. Over the years, it evolved into an annual ritual—most prominently associated with Samhain celebrations—to honor the dead, celebrate rebirth, and emphasize communal solidarity.

During the performance, all members present form a continuous single file, holding hands and following a leader in a counter-clockwise direction using a grapevine step. Accompanied by a drumming group and chant or song, the leader winds the line into a tight inner coil. As the leader approaches the center or closes the circle, they turn around to move clockwise, facing the rest of the moving line. This dynamic reversal ensures that every dancer eventually comes face-to-face with every other participant as the coils pass one another.

In intimate and close-knit circles where participants are comfortable, a kiss or direct eye contact is exchanged at the exact moment dancers pass each other along the winding pathway. In larger or public gatherings, physical kissing may be discouraged to prevent disruptions to the collective rhythm and flow of the step. The physical movement serves as a vessel to raise spiritual energy within a ritual context.

While the ritual lost a large portion of its explicit political focus in subsequent iterations compared to its 1979 debut, it remains a central ceremonial practice within Reclaiming Witches and Neopagan communities. Its performance creates a physical visualization of interweaving lives, shared breath, and recurring cycles of life, death, and renewal.

sections.origins_and_history: The spiral dance was first performed in Berkeley, California, during a 1979 ritual intended to meld art, music, and politics, as well as celebrate the publication of Starhawk's book The Spiral Dance. It grew into a central ritual for Reclaiming Witches and an annual Neopagan tradition in the United States, particularly as a Samhain celebration to honor the dead and celebrate rebirth.
sections.how_it_is_danced: Dancers hold hands in a single line and follow a designated leader using a grapevine step. The leader moves counter-clockwise to form an inner spiral. Upon reaching the interior of the circle, the leader turns around to lead the line clockwise while facing the incoming dancers. This movement weaves the line so every participant passes face-to-face with every other dancer. A beginner starts by joining hands in line and maintaining the rhythm of the grapevine step behind the person ahead.
sections.music_and_instruments: The dance is performed to live music typically featuring a drumming group accompanied by vocal chants or songs to maintain rhythm and raise ritual energy.
sections.costume_and_setting: The dance is performed in communal ritual spaces or outdoor circles during Neopagan gatherings and annual Samhain rituals. Specific standard costumes are not detailed in sources.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: The dance is performed to raise power in a ritual, emphasize community, and mark occasions such as Samhain to honor the dead and celebrate rebirth.
sections.notable_figures: Starhawk, author of the 1979 book The Spiral Dance, whose publication launch ritual established the dance tradition.
sections.regional_variants: Variants depend on circle size and intimacy: close-knit circles may incorporate a kiss exchanged between passing dancers, whereas large public rituals discourage kissing to maintain structural rhythm.
sections.lineage: Developed within 1970s feminist Wicca and the Reclaiming movement in California as a ceremonial group ritual.

profile.sacred_note: The Spiral Dance is a Neopagan ritual practice used to raise power and honor the dead. Intimacy customs like kissing depend on participant consent and circle norms; rhythm and boundary respect should be maintained.

basic_steps: Join hands with neighbors to form a connected line.
Execute a rhythmic grapevine step continuously.
Follow the leader counter-clockwise as the line coils inward.
Turn 180 degrees with the leader to face passing dancers and move clockwise outward.
teaching.rhythm: Steady rhythmic pulse driven by live drumming and collective chant.
teaching.formation: Single-file line holding hands, coiling counter-clockwise into a spiral and uncoiling clockwise.
teaching.level_notes: Accessible to beginners; relies on maintaining line contact and grapevine footwork.

music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Rhythmic pulse supported by drumming group and singing
music_profile.vocal_style: Chant or song sung by participants and music group
music_profile.musical_form: Continuous repetitive ritual chant accompanying physical winding
music_profile.sound_description: Live collective percussion and group chant that builds momentum as the spiral winds and unwinds.

movement_profile.posture: Upright, connected hand-to-hand in a continuous line.
movement_profile.footwork: Grapevine step used throughout the progression.
movement_profile.arms_and_hands: All members present hold hands continuously along the line.
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Facing along the path of movement, pivoting 180 degrees at the central turn.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Single file line entering in counter-clockwise spiral, turning inward to uncoil clockwise face-to-face.
movement_profile.partnering: Connected line holding hands; brief face-to-face encounters with passing line members (sometimes including a kiss).

signature_moves.name: Grapevine line step
signature_moves.description: Side-stepping footwork carrying the connected line in counter-clockwise and clockwise spirals.

signature_moves.name: The Center Turn
signature_moves.description: The leader turns around near the center of the spiral to face the incoming line and lead them back out clockwise.

movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Breaking hand contacts, disrupting line spacing, or forcing unwanted physical intimacy during face-to-face passes.

prerequisites.description: Ability to perform a side-stepping grapevine movement in synchronization with a group line.

social_formats.description: Connected group line holding hands led by a single leader coiling and uncoiling.
